Every year my extended family does a gift exchange around the holidays.
And every year, without fail, somebody's careful wrapping job gets mixed up with somebody else's completely different gift.
This year, I'd spent actual time picking out something nice for my aunt, a set of nice tea and a little journal.
I wrapped it carefully in paper I'd specifically bought to match her favorite color, a soft lavender she'd mentioned liking months earlier.
My cousin, apparently, had wrapped a gag gift for our uncle in nearly identical paper, some ridiculous inflatable flamingo pool float.
It was purely a joke, tied to an ongoing argument they'd been having all year.
Somehow, during the chaos of everyone piling gifts under the tree, the tags fell off both.
The wrapping looked close enough that nobody thought twice about handing them to the wrong people.
We always just grab random gifts instead of checking names, so honestly, this should have felt less surprising.
My aunt unwrapped her gift, and out came a giant inflatable flamingo.
For a solid five seconds, the entire room just stared, completely unsure what to make of the situation unfolding in front of us.
Meanwhile, my uncle unwrapped a delicate tea set and a thoughtful journal.
He blinked at it like he'd just been handed a very confusing peace offering instead of the joke gift he was expecting.
He kept turning the journal over in his hands, genuinely confused.
He kept glancing between the tea set and my cousin, like he was trying to figure out what he'd done to deserve something this nice from her this year.
My aunt, to her credit, held up the flamingo with a completely straight face.
She announced it was "exactly what she'd always wanted." That got the whole room laughing hard enough that someone actually cried a little, wiping tears away between fits of laughter.
We eventually sorted out the actual gifts and swapped them properly.
My uncle insisted on keeping the flamingo too, saying two gifts was clearly the correct outcome of this whole mix-up.
Nobody in the room had the energy left to argue with him about it, and honestly, at that point, nobody really wanted to.
Now, every single gift gets a name tag taped directly onto the item itself, not just looped around with string.
Apparently our family cannot be trusted with matching wrapping paper two years running.
My cousin still insists she's keeping her flamingo forever now too.
She says it's officially become part of the family holiday decorations, and honestly, nobody has bothered arguing with her about it since that whole chaotic afternoon.
It shows up in the family photos every single year now, propped right next to the tree.
